This license text has numerous issues, including non-ideomatic language, 
the "grant" waiving all rights to *all* intellectual property, whether 
or not it relates at all to the content to which it is attached, and a 
likely non-functional (at least in the USA) disclaimer of liability. 
There are other issues as well.

Although you say you've "tried your best" without the use of a lawyer, I 
think if you want to propose something that has any chance of being 
useable, and approvable, you'd likely need to have the help of a lawyer. 
Waivers/disclaimers of IP rights are quite complex, particularly given 
international laws in that regard, and trying to do this on your own 
isn't likely to result in something functional.

Public domain equivalent licenses are a category:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public-domain-equivalent_license

My entry in that category (a dozen years ago) was "Zero Clause BSD" 
(BSD0) which I got approved by SPDX a few months before somebody else 
submitted it here under a different name and caused various headaches. I 
walked it through the github choose-a-license approval process in 2018 
and it's in reasonably widespread use:

https://github.com/search?q=license%3A0bsd&type=Repositories&ref=advsearch&l=&l
If done properly (my understanding is) public domain equivalent licenses 
are the only license type that's fungible, so you can pull in code from 
multiple differently public domain equivalent licensed sources without 
"the stuttering problem" of having to list multiple licenses on your 
codebase (and then having your source control history supoenaed to see 
what license applies to what lines of code if you ever wind up having it 
enforced). This is because this license category does NOT require you to 
copy the license text into derived works, but just grants permissions 
(and optionally disclaims liability).

That means, if there's a public domain equivalent license in use not 
just by open source developers but by google, microsoft, and facebook 
(all of which not just ship but author software under 0BSD)... could you 
explain why you're doing another one?

Rob

Hi, I read your draft license, and I think the waiver is far too broad. As
written, it could easily backfire and, in my view, isn't practical to use.

One issue is that the license appears to waive trademark rights, which
doesn't make sense. Trademark law is fundamentally different from copyright
and patents. The whole purpose of a trademark is to preserve the exclusive
right to use a name or mark in commerce. Most open source and
source-available licenses don't waive trademark rights; instead, they
simply state that the license does not grant any permission to use the
licensor's trademarks.

More broadly, the waiver language is so expansive that it could be
interpreted as a general waiver of the licensor's rights, rather than a
limited waiver for a specific purpose. That creates unnecessary ambiguity
and could produce unintended legal consequences.

This isn't legal advice, but I think the waiver should be narrowed
substantially and should expressly exclude trademark rights rather than
attempting to waive them.

Hi AMOGUSForever,

I took a look at your draft of the *Universal Public Domain License 1.5.2*
and made a few improvements that you might want to consider. I think they
help clarify the intent of the license and avoid a few potential legal
issues.

Of course, I'm *not a lawyer*, and *this is not legal advice*. These are
just drafting suggestions based on my own understanding, so please review
them carefully and use whatever you think is appropriate.

I've included the complete revised draft below.
The Universal Public Domain License 1.5.2

*Public Domain Dedication*

Copyright © [year] [Creator]

*NO RIGHTS RESERVED!*
§1. Waiver

To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the Creator irrevocably
dedicates the Work to the public domain and waives all copyright and
related rights, together with any patent rights owned or controlled by the
Creator to the extent necessary to permit unrestricted use of the Work,
worldwide.

Without limitation, this dedication and waiver includes the right to
reproduce, use, copy, modify, adapt, merge, publish, distribute, perform,
display, communicate, translate, sublicense, and sell the Work:

   -

   for the maximum duration permitted by applicable law, including any
   future extensions;
   -

   in every present and future medium or format;
   -

   for any purpose whatsoever, including commercial purposes;
   -

   all moral rights, to the extent they may be waived or not asserted under
   applicable law;
   -

   all neighbouring or related rights;
   -

   all publicity, privacy, and personality rights relating to any person
   depicted in the Work;
   -

   all rights protecting against unfair competition relating to the Work;
   -

   all rights protecting the extraction, dissemination, use, and reuse of
   data contained in the Work;
   -

   all database rights and similar rights under any jurisdiction; and
   -

   all equivalent or corresponding intellectual property rights now
   existing or hereafter created under any applicable law or treaty.

For the avoidance of doubt, trademark, service mark, trade name, trade
dress, and other rights identifying the source of goods or services are
neither waived nor licensed under this License.

The same dedication and waiver apply to this License document itself.
§2. Permissive License Fallback

If, under applicable law, the public domain dedication or any waiver
described in Section 1 is ineffective, invalid, or unenforceable, in whole
or in part, each rights holder hereby grants every recipient a perpetual,
worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable license to exercise all
rights that the rights holder has, or may hereafter acquire, in the Work
under any intellectual property rights identified in Section 1, including,
without limitation, the rights to reproduce, use, copy, modify, adapt,
merge, publish, distribute, perform, display, communicate, translate,
sublicense, and sell the Work, for any purpose, including commercial
purposes.
§3. Disclaimer

THE WORK IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, OR NON-INFRINGEMENT.

TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
CREATOR, ANY CONTRIBUTOR, OR ANY COPYRIGHT, RELATED RIGHTS, OR PATENT
HOLDER BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES, OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN
ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT, OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF, OR IN
CONNECTION WITH THE WORK OR THE USE OF OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE WORK.
§4. Severability

If any provision of this License is held to be invalid, illegal, or
unenforceable under applicable law, that provision shall be reformed or
enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law, and if it cannot be so
reformed or enforced, it shall be severed from this License without
affecting the validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions.
------------------------------

I hope some of these changes are useful. Feel free to use, modify, or
ignore any of them as you see fit. and consult with lawyer
